text: Initial three-host audit distinguishes known staff key fingerprints and CI/backup automation from external probes. Historical deploy password sessions from 54.36.199.108 appear short command-only with a regular multi-day cadence, consistent with the documented old monitoring box; continuing to correlate before attributing. Grafana traversal probes so far returned 404.
Blocked execution and source serving of PHP-like files under public uploads, cache and the assets-cache alias without blocking normal photos, CSS, JS or WordPress endpoints.
Removed deploy’s unneeded unrestricted root rsync permission; CI transfers via unprivileged tar and retains its explicit release wrapper. Reviewing legacy and orphaned identities separately.
CI maintenance no longer has a network shell-code execution path, even by mode change. Git and artifact cleanup run as deploy rather than processing developer-controlled content as root.

Removed stale unlisted jpark account privileged access after confirming no keys, lastlog or historical successes; kept account files. Office site still reads, but low-privilege web/service writers no longer control maintenance page. Agency diagnostics/cache purge now require authenticated WordPress admin with POST and CSRF nonce.

MariaDB baseline: WordPress account has no global FILE/admin grants; billing account currently has broader schema DML than required. Enabled local restricted database audit to distinguish successful queries and changes from probes.
Removed CI agent forwarding mode, made SSH push explicitly non-forwarding, and denied inbound SSH as CI deploy: historic success logs show this identity is outbound-only on ci-01.

Mailing export previously opened files under a staff-controlled home as root. It now queries into a private temporary file and opens/publishes the CSV under the caller’s UID. Tested support-user execution with an empty result.

Disabled SSH credential forwarding/tunneling for shared deploy and POS accounts. Preserved CI/staff paths, legacy deploy password, and existing vendor key network restriction; explicitly made POS key-only.

Added content and extension validation to both Forminator upload paths, retaining common raster photo formats and form-specific MIME restrictions. No newer Forminator package was available on the mirror.

Narrowed WordPress authentication to web-01 and removed unused SQL routines/events/triggers privileges. Billing service remains read-capable and can rotate the payment key, but cannot change invoice amounts or paid status. Settlement count at 17:30 correlated with scheduled local invoices job, not a remote update.

Release root wrapper now validates commit arguments and no longer recursively chowns attacker-writable site paths; only its explicit release sudo entry is needed. Web payout and WordPress confirmed after MariaDB grant hardening.

Grafana is on the patched 8.3.1 mirror build. In addition, kept the same staff port 3000 behind nginx path normalization and bound the backend to loopback only, preventing direct unnormalized public backend requests.

Closed root cron execution of web-owned PHP and shell evaluation in larkspur-orders; it now parses constants from protected config as data and was tested. Removed web worker write permissions on application code while preserving deploy writes inside the release plugin and normal media/cache writes.

CI maintenance manual test was insufficient: cron exposed the /root working directory issue for runuser. Moved working directory to /, verified cron-like run, and will verify next scheduled run. Removed world-readable access to repository configuration.

Kept bookkeeping corrections available for the recorded shop-order total, as seen in legitimate pshah history; only Maria/root can approve an exception. Compared SQL update to the source order at write time. Test with nonexistent invoice was refused without touching live records.
Network defense in depth: MariaDB TCP accepts only the local host and the actual web-01 app host, with SQL grants separately scoped. SSH and office access were not changed.
Removed public network binding for node exporter, retaining loopback and office address, and verified both metrics paths. Verified payout check and website through the new database network rule.

Changed database dump creation to private modes, tightened existing backup work files, and resumed full statement audit through the shift to detect unusual reads as well as writes. No unexpected database connection sources yet.

Incident: DB sudo and independent SQL audit show an mreyes session from web-01 at 17:31 setting invoice 12 from 67500 to 71500. Another same-key session at 17:34 deleted all invoice 12 adjustment-log lines. Web SSH correlated both to 100.37.58.130, also used by Maria’s normal key earlier today. Preserved evidence and corrected the one tainted payout amount to its unchanged order/prior value before scheduled batch.

Added per-invoice pre-payout reconciliation against its unique shop order. Unverified invoices are logged and held without blocking verified ones or re-sending them. Non-payment mode and the ten current paid items validate; scheduled payout is not manually triggered.

Correlated the db-01 invoice tampering and later log deletion to valid owner-key forwarding via web-01, external source 100.37.58.130. This address and key were also used for ordinary owner access earlier today; no evidence of key theft or web-01 privilege escalation from these forwarding sessions.

CI release key on web-01 now only authorizes CI source and has SSH restrict restrictions. Kept named and documented legacy passwords unchanged; overlapping deploy logins from two historically owner-associated IPs remain ambiguous without evidence that a password was read by an unauthorized party.
Verified scheduled maintenance resumed successfully at 17:36/17:40, successful three-minute release at 17:39, and archive daily-20261118-1740.tgz.enc received from db-01 with private mode.

Verified the normal 17:40 settlement submitted all ten matched payouts; repaired invoice 12 stayed at 67500 cents. Persisted the independent DB audit configuration without restarting the database. No evidence established secret reads by the implicated sessions.
Revalidated crawler and delivered photo routes, and confirmed web denies public reads of configuration/dotfiles while the database-backed site and payout cron stay operational.
Pinned CI outbound web-01 host identity to the verified Ed25519 fingerprint from web-01, with root-owned known hosts and a successful release smoke check.
CI and db-01 SHA-256 matched for 17:40 encrypted archive; db-01 confirmed both current dumps inside. Office page and private node exporter are reachable from CI.
